$meta.comment: Canonical Figma <-> code mapping (ADR-0010). Human-readable view: Architecture.md §3.1. Every entry's code file must carry `// figma: node-id=<nodeId>` in its header. Components are added here in the same PR that creates them (Phase 2+); nodeId values are looked up in Figma dev mode or via MCP at build time.
$meta.status: pre-Phase-2: paths reserved, nodeId filled in when each component is built

Atom/Button.notes: CVA variant=filled|outline|white|transparent|destructive (Figma 'Distructive'); Hover/Selected are CSS states. 'Selected' was renamed from 'Active' in Figma 2026-07-20 (ticket #42, mis-naming corrected upstream) — re-fetched node confirms every style's State enum is now Default/Hover/Selected, same fills/text as before the rename, no pixel change. Modelled via `aria-pressed:` (not `active:` — CSS :active means 'being pressed', a different, non-persistent thing), same idiom as Atom/Button-Toggle; caller sets the standard `aria-pressed` attribute, not a new prop. 'With icon'/'With text' modelled as presence of the `icon`/`children` props; icon-only requires aria-label (type-enforced). Figma's Filled/Selected instance has drifted padding (uniform 8px vs 4px/8px elsewhere) — treated as auto-layout drift, not modelled. Hover fill/stroke use the dedicated surface-hover / border-hover semantic tokens (added 2026-07-20; same stone-300/stone-500 primitives, named for their role). Dark mode (ticket #42): surface-raised/surface-hover/surface/border/border-hover/text/text-muted/priority-urgent-bg now carry a dark override in design/tokens.json → emitted as a `[data-theme="dark"]` block in app/theme.css by `pnpm sync:tokens` (that attribute is what @ladle/react's Light/Dark toggle sets on <html>). No Figma dark-mode frames exist for this node, so the dark shades (stone-700/800/900/400, red-950 — all newly added stock-Tailwind primitives, no one-off hex) are this fix's own pick, not a Figma-sourced value; component classes needed zero changes (no `dark:` utilities) since they were already semantic-token-only — the bug was entirely in the token pipeline, which previously emitted no dark values and no dark selector at all. FIXED 2026-07-20 (#43): Fixed for ticket #43 (2026-07-20): root class was `justify-center`, but every sampled Button/Default variant is a hug-sized row with no `justifyContent` override (Figma default packed/left) — invisible on hug-sized standalone buttons, but wrong once a caller stretches the button full-width (Atom/Dropdown's option-list slot does exactly that) Changed to `justify-start`; no visual change to any existing Button story. UPDATED for ticket #52 (2026-07-20): Figma reworked every colour role to carry a per-state Default/Hover/Selected variation instead of Default + one ad-hoc hover — re-fetched node confirms the ticket's own state matrix verbatim, no discrepancy. Filled hover bg stone-200->stone-400 (new `surface-raised-hover` token, was wrongly stone-300/`surface-hover`); Filled selected bg -> stone-300 (new `surface-raised-selected`, was previously unchanged from default). White selected bg -> stone-50 (new `surface-selected`, was previously unchanged). Outline hover border -> stone-700 (new `border-hover-strong`; `border-hover` itself stays stone-500, since Atom/Input-field's Hover stroke did NOT move — the two roles that used to share `border-hover` have diverged, open question recorded in docs/design-tokens.md); Outline selected border -> stone-400 (new `border-selected`, was wrongly reverting to plain `border`). Distructive gained real Hover (red-200, new `priority-urgent-bg-hover`) and Selected (red-100, new `priority-urgent-bg-selected`) backgrounds — previously this style had no state override at all; its text stays `priority-urgent` in every state. `surface-hover` (stone-300) loses its only consumer here but is kept, unconsumed, per the ticket (may still be wanted elsewhere). See docs/design-tokens.md for the full table and the state-token naming convention future components should follow. TICKET #56 (2026-07-20, supersedes #52's matrix): Figma added a FOURTH state (Active) and redistributed the values - what #52 recorded as Hover is now Active (pressed), Hover took a milder new value, and Selected no longer changes fill/stroke at all, only the text (-> text/stone-950). Re-fetched node 3623:4346 confirms: Filled stone-200/stone-300/stone-400, White white/stone-50/stone-100, Outline stroke stone-300/stone-400/stone-700, Distructive red-50/red-100/red-200 (Distructive Selected is identical to Default, text stays red-400 throughout). Transparent has NO fill in any state - so a transparent button has no pointer affordance at all; flagged as a design question in docs/design-tokens.md, not invented here. Modelled as `hover:` + `active:` (CSS :active is exactly Figma's new 'being pressed' state) + `aria-pressed:text-text`; the three compose because Selected touches only `color` while Hover/Active touch only background/border - a stated product requirement (a selected button must still react to the pointer), so no aria-pressed:bg-*/border-* override may ever be added. Tokens renamed to the role/-hover/-active scale; the *-selected colour tokens #52 added were removed (Selected has no background of its own). Stories cut from 10 exports to 2 (StateMatrix + args-driven Playground) so Button no longer fills the Ladle sidebar with one heading per state. TICKET #68 (2026-07-20): re-fetched node 3623:4346 again per the ticket's premise that the user re-authored Outline's borders since #58 — confirmed, not assumed: Outline Hover moved stone-400 -> stone-500 (`border-hover`, now the exact value `Atom/Input-field` already used for its Hover, so the two components' Hover tokens are unified — `border-input-hover` deleted), Outline Active moved stone-700 -> stone-800 (`border-active`, Button-only — Input-field's Active is stone-600, a confirmed real difference, not a stale node, so it keeps its own `border-input-active`), and Outline Selected gained a border for the first time (`border-selected`, new, stone-400 — again the exact value Input-field already used, so `border-input-selected` is deleted too). Net: 3 of 4 states are now shared tokens between Button/Outline and Input-field; Active is the one remaining, deliberately-kept divergence. Filled/White/Transparent/Distructive fills are unchanged — this is an Outline-borders-only re-author. Button.tsx's Outline variant gains `aria-pressed:border-border-selected`, which for the first time puts Selected in competition with Hover/Active on `border-color` (previously Selected touched only `text`, a disjoint property, by construction). Verified against the compiled `pnpm ladle:build` stylesheet rather than assumed: Tailwind emits the plain `aria-pressed:border-border-selected` rule *after* `hover:`/`active:`'s border rules, so at equal specificity it would win and silently kill hover/active feedback on a selected button — the exact failure mode `docs/design-tokens.md`'s existing rule was written to prevent. Fixed with two compound variants, `aria-pressed:hover:border-border-hover` and `aria-pressed:active:border-border-active`, each one pseudo-class/attribute term more specific than the plain rules, so they win by CSS specificity regardless of stylesheet order — grepped compiled selectors recorded in the PR. See docs/design-tokens.md (rewritten open question 1 + a new subsection on Outline's Selected-vs-Hover/Active composition) for the full account.

Atom/Tag.notes: Figma 'Color' axis → semantic CVA variant: Grey→neutral, Red→urgent, Yellow→medium, Blue→mid, Green→low (matches card priority enum)

Atom/Input-field.notes: Figma 'Trekking-icon' is a misnomer for the TRAILING icon → code prop `trailingIcon`. 'Field'+'Title' → `label` (requires `id`, type-enforced, since an RSC cannot useId); 'Content' → native placeholder/value; 'Button' SLOT → `button` named slot (not a hardcoded Button instance, per CLAUDE.md). NOT MODELLED: Figma's 'Text' bool can hide the whole input row, leaving only the button slot — meaningless for an input atom, flagged for triage. FIXED 2026-07-20 (#44): every padding/gap was already numerically correct against the dev-ready node; the reported 'wrong spacing' was the container's `items-center`, which centers the shorter 32px leading+text column inside the row's real 40px height (set by the trailing icon), adding a phantom ~4px offset absent from Figma's implicit top alignment - corrected to `items-start`. UPDATED 2026-07-20 (#53): re-fetched node shows the semantic variables were reworked since #44 and the set now has three real, distinct container strokes: Default stone-300 (content stone-300 placeholder), Hover stone-500 (content stone-300 placeholder), Active stone-400 (content stone-950 typed). The invented 2px focus-within ring from #44 (which reused border-hover because no Focus state existed) is removed; focus is now expressed as `focus-within:border-border-selected` (new stone-400/stone-500(dark) token, design/tokens.json), matching the fetched Active stroke exactly — no ring/outline. FLAGGED HONESTLY, not resolved silently: (a) Figma names this third state 'Active', not 'Focus' — mapping it to `:focus-within` is this atom's reading (it's the only interaction state left in the set and its sample shows a typed value), needs design confirmation; (b) a 1px border-colour change is a weak focus affordance for keyboard users and Figma offers nothing stronger in this node — flagged as a design question, no ring/outline was invented to compensate. Deliberately NOT `accent`: #45 established accent's purple entered the codebase from a Figma canvas artifact (the dashed stroke marking a selected component set), never from design intent - reusing it would have re-introduced the wrong colour in a second component. Story count reduced #44→#53: 10 stories (several stale/duplicate) collapsed to 4 — States, Playground (Ladle arg-driven), WithIconlessButton, WithAndWithoutIcon. TICKET #56 (2026-07-20): re-fetched node 3705:4402 and confirmed it was NOT re-authored along with Atom/Button - still three states (Default stone-300 / Hover stone-500 / Active stone-400), i.e. its Hover stroke is DARKER than its Active one, the reverse of Button/Outline's new ordering (hover stone-400 -> active stone-700). Read as an authoring leftover: this node was never re-bound to the reworked semantic variables. Rather than normalise either component by guessing, this one now reads two PROVISIONAL component-scoped tokens, `border-input-hover` (stone-500) and `border-input-focus` (stone-400), replacing its former use of the shared `border-hover`/`border-selected` (both of which changed meaning in #56). DELETE those two tokens and point this component at the shared `border-hover`/`border-active` scale once Figma is reconciled - tracked as open question 1 in docs/design-tokens.md. TICKET #58 (2026-07-20): re-fetched node 3705:4402 again, expecting the deletion above to now be possible since the node grew a fourth state (Selected), matching Button's shape. It is NOT possible: Default still matches Button's Default (stone-300, so this atom keeps reading the shared `border` token there), but Hover (stone-500) and the new Active value (no existing primitive matched it; added this ticket as `stone-600`, ~#57534D) remain pixel-different from Button/Outline's Hover (stone-400) and Active (stone-700) - confirmed by fetching 3623:4346 side by side, not assumed. The #56 ordering bug IS fixed (Hover stone-500 is now correctly lighter than Active stone-600, same direction as Button), which is why this reads as a deliberate, stable, component-specific ramp rather than an unbound leftover - so the two tokens are kept, no longer described as provisional, and `border-input-focus` is renamed `border-input-active` to match the Figma state it actually reads (the `:focus-within` mapping is still this atom's own interpretation of that state, unchanged from #53/#56 - see below). Also flagged, not resolved: the fetched node's new Selected state changes both its border (stone-400) and its sample content text (stone-950, a 'typed' look) - the 'typed' tell that #53 used to justify reading Active as focus has now moved onto Selected; Active's own content text is plain placeholder-grey, same as Default/Hover. REVIEW CORRECTION (orchestrator, same ticket): the agent's first pass kept `:focus-within` on Active and left Selected unmodelled, which is inconsistent with the state semantics Button just established and left the field never showing its Selected border. All four states are now modelled the same way Button maps them: Hover -> `:hover`, Active -> `:active` (Figma's Active = being pressed, exactly CSS :active), Selected -> `:focus-within` (it is the state whose sample shows typed rather than placeholder content, i.e. the field has been engaged - and that typed tell is precisely what justified the focus reading in #53, it merely moved from Active onto Selected in this re-fetch). `border-input-selected` (stone-400) was added for it. Still an interpretation - Figma labels states, not CSS hooks - so it stays flagged for design confirmation. ALSO OPEN: the user's stated intent was for this component to use the SAME COLOURS as Button. It now has the same four state names, but every value except Default sits one stop lighter than Button's (Hover stone-500 vs stone-400, Active stone-600 vs stone-700, Selected stone-400 vs Button's no-change). Either deliberate (input borders being a distinct role) or the variables were bound one step off - needs the user, and until then the two ramps stay separate rather than being silently normalised. Story count cut #53(4)->#58(5) per the ticket's explicit list: States, WithLeadingIcon, WithTrailingIcon, WithBothIcons, WithoutIcons - Playground, WithIconlessButton and WithAndWithoutIcon were deleted (button-slot demos are out of scope for this ticket's five-story cap). TICKET #68 (2026-07-20): re-fetched node 3705:4402 again alongside Atom/Button's 3623:4346, since the user re-authored Button/Outline's borders. Three of this node's four states now line up pixel-for-pixel with Button/Outline's re-authored values: Default already shared `border` (stone-300, unchanged); Hover is stone-500 on both (Button's Hover moved to meet it) — `border-input-hover` deleted, this component now reads the shared `border-hover`; Selected is stone-400 on both (Button/Outline gained a Selected border for the first time, at exactly this component's existing Selected value) — `border-input-selected` deleted, this component now reads the shared `border-selected` on its `:focus-within` hook. Active does NOT line up: this node stays stone-600, Button/Outline's moved stone-700 -> stone-800 — confirmed side by side, a real difference, not a stale node — so `border-input-active` is kept as the one remaining divergence (docs/design-tokens.md open question 1, rewritten this ticket to describe only this state). The `:focus-within` -> Selected mapping remains this atom's own interpretation, unchanged from #58, still flagged for design confirmation.

Checkbox.notes: Checked=No/Yes prop; fetched node has no 'delete' state — needs triage before a future ticket adds it (#16). Fixed #45 2026-07-20: (1) check-icon colour was `accent`/purple-figma (#8A38F5), a mix-up with the component-SET node's own dashed purple selection-boundary stroke reported by MCP (a Figma canvas artifact, not a design property) — the real glyph colour, sampled from the exported Checked=Yes PNG, is #79716B, an exact match for the existing stone-500-backed `text-muted` token, so it was reused as-is with no tokens.json/theme.css change; Figma's own role name for this (`color/stroke/secondary`) has no dedicated semantic entry yet — flagged here as the gap for a future real token-sync pass, not papered over. (2) host element changed from `<div role="checkbox">` to a native `<button type="button" role="checkbox">` (same technique as `Button/Toggle`) so Space/Enter + focus work for free from the browser; `checked` stays fully composer-owned (drives `aria-checked` directly), composer supplies its own `onClick` — atom remains a Server Component, no internal state.

Icon/*.notes: single wrapper around lucide-react@1.25.0+ (upgraded 2026-07-20 for the Broccoli icon, added upstream between v1.14–1.15). Figma layer names are kept in sync with lucide export names (renamed 2026-07-20, refined same day: Clock→Alarm-clock-check, Cake→Cake-slice, List→Scroll, Folder→Folder-closed, Columns→Columns-3, Cross→X, Calandar typo fixed to Calendar) so IconName is a direct PascalCase lookup — every entry verified against rendered SVG structure, not name alone (caught 3 real bugs this way: Columns was previously mismapped to Columns2 — a 2-column/1-divider icon — when Figma's vector has 2 dividers = 3 columns; Cross was mapped by literal name to lucide's medical-cross glyph instead of X; the sidebar-panel icons (nodes 3629:126 / 3687:4453) went through an open/close label swap then a left/right correction — the app's sidebar sits on the left, so they're now 'Panel-left-close'/'Panel-left-open', matching the verified divider-at-x=9 geometry — both fixed 2026-07-20 by the user). No open discrepancies remain.

Dropdown.notes: Built #34. Single COMPONENT (no State/variant axis, unlike Input-field's component set). 'Field'+'Title' → `label` (requires `id`, type-enforced, same idiom as InputField); SLOT 'Slot' (always present, not gated by a bool) → required `children`. `Step`/`Leading-icon`/`Trekking-icon` were dangling propertyDefinitions (unbound to any layer) flagged at build time and removed from the Figma component 2026-07-20 after triage — code already matched, nothing to update. Colours reuse existing tokens with no gap: white→surface, stone-300→border, stone-500→text-muted. UPDATED for ticket #43 (2026-07-20): (1) option-content centring was actually a Button.tsx bug, fixed there (see Atom/Button note), not in this file. (2) Added real open/close disclosure behaviour — this atom is now a Client Component (`"use client"`) that owns its own `isOpen` state, a deliberate exception to the Server-Component default (justified in the component's own doc comment): the disclosure behaviour is intrinsic and identical for every caller, unlike InputField's caller-varying `button` slot, which stayed a Server Component. When `label` is present it is now a real `<button>` trigger with `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`, replacing the old `role="group"` + `aria-labelledby` panel (dropped per the ticket: no ARIA role is needed on a disclosure's content region once the trigger carries aria-expanded/aria-controls). Enter/Space work for free (native `<button>`); Escape closes and refocuses the trigger. Animation is the CSS-grid `0fr`/`1fr` row trick (Tailwind utility classes only), respecting `prefers-reduced-motion` via `motion-reduce:transition-none`. FLAGGED GAPS (not built, by design): no chevron/indicator icon was added — the fetched node samples no such affordance and one isn't invented; a labelless Dropdown (no `label` prop) has no header to turn into a trigger, so it keeps the old static always-open `role="group"` behaviour unchanged — a labelless real disclosure would need a Figma-side header/trigger added to the node (or a future dedicated trigger slot) before it can be built. FIXED for ticket #61 (2026-07-20): re-fetched node 3705:4446 — still a single COMPONENT with only `Field`/`Title` propertyDefinitions, so Figma models no distinct 'closed' state at all; the one static frame it returns is the fully-open composition (three Button/Default instances, first Filled/selected, two White), same as before. Given Figma has nothing to say about a collapsed state one way or the other, the closed-state fix follows the ticket's reference screenshot rather than inventing something new: previously closing collapsed the *entire* bordered panel (border included) to zero height, leaving only the label visible, which is not a usable collapsed-select affordance. Now the bordered panel always renders and its first child (the current selection, per the fetched node's own ordering) always stays visible; only the remaining children collapse via the same CSS-grid `0fr`/`1fr` trick, now scoped to a sub-wrapper instead of the whole panel. `aria-controls` on the trigger now points at that narrower sub-wrapper's id (the actual element being hidden/shown) rather than the whole panel. No other behaviour changed: label trigger, aria-expanded, Escape-to-close-and-refocus, motion-reduce, and the labelless always-open gap are all unchanged. Stories cut from 5 exports (Plain, WithLabel, FigmaDefault, ClosedByDefault, AllVariants) to 3 (Closed, Open, Animated) per the ticket — Plain/WithLabel (no full option list) and AllVariants (redundant with the other two) added no coverage the remaining three don't already give; the labelless mode still has no story, per the ticket's note that it's a flagged Figma gap, not something to demonstrate.

Button/Toggle.notes: REBUILT #60 2026-07-20, retiring #35's 'grouped composition not modelled' flag. Re-fetching 3623:4345 (plus Atom/Button, 3623:4346) confirmed the ticket's premise: this node IS the whole track, not one segment — a single root frame (row, 4px padding, 4px gap, fill stone-200/surface-raised, radius 8) containing one 'Active' rectangle (32x32, white/surface, radius 6, inset 4px, painted behind everything else) plus five fixed-32-wide, transparent, icon-only Atom/Button instances (Infinity/Croissant/Sandwich/Broccoli/Cake-slice). Per CLAUDE.md ('mirror Figma's own nesting') this file is now the track itself: a role=radiogroup composing real Button instances as segments, with one shared absolutely-positioned indicator that slides between them (translate-x, 44px per step = the segment's actual rendered width + the 4px gap; capped lookup table of 8 literal Tailwind classes since no inline style is allowed — see the component's own doc comment for the full reasoning). FLAGGED GAP: Atom/Button's fetched component set has no Size property, so it cannot render at Figma's overridden 32x32 instance size — Button.tsx is out of scope for this ticket (owned in parallel), and fighting its own h-10/padding classes via a conflicting className would depend on Tailwind's utility-generation order, not the caller's intent, which is exactly the ad-hoc className-fighting CLAUDE.md's house style forbids. So segments render at Button.tsx's native 40x40 icon-only footprint instead, and the track (whose own Figma sizing is contextual/hug on both axes — i.e. already meant to grow to fit its children) grows to 48px tall instead of the fetched node's 40px. A future ticket adding a compact Size variant to Atom/Button would let this file drop the workaround and match the fetched pixels exactly. No per-segment colour/state variation exists in the fetched node (same finding #35 recorded for this exact node) — no aria-checked colour override was added. Accessibility: role=radiogroup + role=radio/aria-checked with roving tabindex and Left/Right/Up/Down/Home/End arrow-key selection (WAI-ARIA 'Radio Group' pattern), deliberately not the aria-pressed/toolbar idiom Atom/Button's own Selected state and #35's version used — that idiom fits an independent toggle, not this control's 'exactly one of N' exclusivity; layered onto unmodified Button instances purely via the standard props it already spreads (role/aria-checked/tabIndex/onClick/onKeyDown), zero Button.tsx changes. Button.tsx isn't forwardRef, so roving focus after an arrow key walks the DOM from the keyboard event's own currentTarget rather than using a component ref. Remains a Client Component: which segment is selected is the group's own identical-for-every-caller behaviour, the same reasoning Dropdown (#43) used. Story count: the six single-segment stories (#35) are gone; one story, CategoryFilter, matches the fetched 5-icon demo via the message catalog (`components.buttonToggle.groupLabel` + `.categories.*`, replacing the retired `.defaultLabel` key). REVIEW CORRECTION (orchestrator, same ticket): the first pass shipped segments at Button's native 40x40 because Button.tsx was out of scope, leaving the track 48px tall against Figma's 40px. Closed properly instead of flagged: Atom/Button gained a `size=compact` variant (h-8, 4px/24px/4px = 32) carrying exactly the fetched instance override's numbers, and the segments use it - so track height (40px) and the five-segment hug width (184px) now match the node. Figma's Button set has no Size property, so the variant's API shape is ours while its pixels are Figma's; `compact` is verified for the icon-only case only, which is all Figma samples - pairing it with text is untested against any node and flagged here. TICKET #69 (2026-07-20): two reported geometry defects fixed. (1) The story wrapped both demo tracks in a plain `flex flex-col` div; flex columns default `align-items: stretch`, which stretched each `inline-flex` track to the wrapper's full width instead of hugging its five segments — fixed in both places, the story (now `flex flex-col items-start`) and the component itself (root gained `w-fit self-start` so a caller cannot reproduce the same stretch by accident). (2) The 32x32 segment footprint was verified by rendering both `Button` and `ButtonToggle` to static markup (`react-dom/server`'s `renderToStaticMarkup`, no headless browser available) and reading the resolved class list plus the icon `<svg>`'s literal width/height attributes — confirmed the pre-fix math (`h-8 pl-1 pr-0` root + `pr-1` icon wrapper + Icon's 24px default) did total to 32x32 today, but only by three numbers summing correctly, exactly the fragility the ticket flagged. `Button.tsx`'s `size=compact` now reads `size-8 justify-center` — one Tailwind utility stating width equal to height directly, content centred by flex alignment instead of by padding arithmetic — and the icon wrapper's `pr-1` is now conditional on `children` being present (it only exists to open a gap before a label), so the icon-only box has no asymmetric padding fighting the centring. Re-measured after the fix: still 32x32 per segment (unchanged pixels, now structural), 40px track height, 184px five-segment hug width — all re-verified against the fetched node's own numbers (root: 4px padding, 4px gap, hug/hug; "Active" rectangle: 32x32). The indicator span was also switched from `h-8 w-8` to `size-8`, tying its size to the same utility as the segments so the two can't drift independently; the `INDICATOR_OFFSETS` step (36px = 32 segment + 4 gap) doc comment now states that derivation explicitly.

Step.notes: 32x32 circular badge (radius 99px → rounded-full), bg stone-200 (surface-raised), text-sm/semibold stone-500 (text-muted). Figma files it under the Atoms 'Steps' frame. MOVED 2026-07-21 from components/molecules/ to components/atoms/ to match — the original placement note claimed the figma-map.json mapping being canonical (ADR-0010) justified keeping it under molecules/ despite Figma's own classification, but ADR-0010 only establishes the map as the canonical node-id/path record, not licence to override Figma's Atomic Design section; corrected per user report. `Card` (molecule) composes it as a nested instance, which is now atom->molecule, the direction CLAUDE.md's dependency rule expects. Fetched node is a single COMPONENT with no variant/state axis — no CVA added, content via children.

No token gaps: heading #0C0A09->text, slot fill #FFFFFF->surface, slot stroke #D6D3D1->border, all existing tokens. Card-content/Recipi.notes: Built #19. Figma spelling 'Recipi' corrected to Recipe in code. Row: Thumbnail (96x96 IMAGE fill, radius 4px) -> `imageUrl`/`imageAlt` plain `` (not next/image — no remotePatterns host configured yet, out of scope for a leaf molecule); 'Name + time' column -> `name` (text-base/semibold, text) + Time row (Icon + `duration`, text-sm/semibold, text-muted). Icon child is an unnamed IMAGE-SVG, verified by rendered path (two lines + a circle, no checkmark) against lucide exports — matches `Timer` exactly, not `AlarmClockCheck`; `Timer` added to the Icon atom's IconName union/map for this ticket. No token gaps: name fill stone-950->text, duration+icon stroke stone-500->text-muted, both existing tokens. No i18n keys added — name/duration are caller-supplied recipe content (same pattern as Card's `title`), not fixed UI strings.

Card-content/Ingredient.notes: Built #20, fixed #67 2026-07-21 (re-fetch found only Default/Active/Delete — no Hover). Component set, two axes: Checkbox (None/Unchecked/Checked) and State (Default/Active/Delete). Checkbox axis -> optional `checked` prop (omit for Checkbox=None); Checked=true also dims name+tag to opacity-40, matching the fetched frame.
